title: Silicon Valley Titans Launch Campaign to Bring Ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Back Amid Security Scandal
snippet: Days after resigning over explosive revelations involving an alleged Chinese spy and company subordinates, former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is reportedly weighing a comeback—backed by high-profile tech executives and facing fierce resistance from Washington.
content:
SAN FRANCISCO — Just days after stepping down from Nvidia in the wake of an escalating security and workplace misconduct scandal, co-founder Jensen Huang is reportedly exploring a dramatic return to the helm of the artificial intelligence giant.

According to sources familiar with the matter, a coalition of prominent Silicon Valley executives has mobilized to press Nvidia’s board of directors to reinstate Huang. Allies have reportedly established a strategic 'war room' designed to rally key investors and court support from the White House, a push that Huang is said to endorse.

Tech Heavyweights Rally Behind Huang

The campaign to reinstate Huang has quickly gathered backing from top industry figures. Tesla CEO Elon Musk and Epic Games chief Tim Sweeney have thrown their support behind an open letter urging Nvidia's board to 'Bring Jensen Back.' Simultaneously, major Nvidia shareholders—including Brad Gerstner of Altimeter Capital and Gavin Baker of Atreides Management—publicly urged the board to keep 'all options on the table,' including Huang's return.

Because Huang does not hold a controlling stake in Nvidia, any potential return hinges entirely on the board's decision—a board that has so far announced no formal plans to bring him back.

Fierce Resistance in Washington

While Silicon Valley allies push for Huang’s restoration, federal officials are signaling strong opposition. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called Sunday for a 'dramatic shakeup' at the chipmaker, publicly urging the board to seek fresh, outside leadership.

In television appearances over the weekend, Bessent questioned Nvidia's corporate governance and pressed for clarity on whether the company engaged in illicit sales to artificially boost earnings. He demanded concrete answers within 10 days regarding potential export control violations related to Megaspeed, a Singapore-based firm linked to the scandal. 'If this were a bank and they hadn’t complied like this, the OCC would be in there right now, and a lot of the executives would be removed,' Bessent said.

The scandal has also drawn intense scrutiny from Capitol Hill. Representative Brian Mast, chairman of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, confirmed that Huang has agreed to sit for a closed-door interview with lawmakers in early December.

Espionage Allegations and Workplace Misconduct

Huang’s sudden departure last week followed revelations of multiple extramarital affairs. The executive publicly acknowledged an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Megaspeed, who U.S. intelligence agencies suspect of gathering information for the Chinese government. While Nvidia maintained in a statement that national security secrets were not compromised, federal investigators are examining whether Megaspeed improperly secured high-end Nvidia chips restricted under U.S. trade laws.

Reports subsequently surfaced detailing additional relationships with company personnel, including Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare, and a second unnamed subordinate executive.

Financial Fallout and What Lies Ahead

The governance crisis has rocked Wall Street. Nvidia shares dropped 13% immediately following news of Huang's resignation, extending a decline that has wiped out more than $1.2 trillion in market capitalization since late October.

Nvidia Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress has stepped in as interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent replacement. Reports indicate the board has reached out to Arm CEO Rene Haas as a prospective candidate. With Nvidia scheduled to report quarterly earnings on Tuesday and hold an all-hands employee meeting on Wednesday, the company faces unprecedented scrutiny as it attempts to navigate its biggest crisis in three decades.
